hero.title: For funds, family offices and holding companies with investees
hero.description: Sttok brings together your investees with their percentage, their shares and their value, draws the chain of control on any date and simulates each transaction before it is signed: a capital increase, a note conversion or the waterfall of a sale.

includes.title: What an investor with several investees uses

rows.situation: You need to know what you hold in each company
rows.action: Each investee appears with its percentage, its shares and its book value.
The simulator calculates the price per share, the new shares and each shareholder's dilution.
It calculates the resulting shares and their effect on the other shareholders.

rows.situation: The sale of an investee is being negotiated
rows.action: The liquidation waterfall shows what each shareholder receives, with the preferences of each class.

rows.situation: The committee asks for the group picture at year-end
rows.action: The chart shows the chain of control on any date and what changed between two year-ends.

items.q: Can I see all my investees in one place?
items.a: Yes. They are shown as cards or a table, grouped by relationship, level and country, with their percentage and value.

items.q: Does it calculate my stake when I hold it through several routes?
items.a: Yes. The chart adds up the routes and shows the effective percentage alongside the direct one.

items.q: Can I simulate a capital increase in an investee?
items.a: Yes, on the investee's shareholder register when it is kept in Sttok. A simulation records nothing.

items.q: Can I request my investees' filed accounts?
items.a: Yes. Sttok requests them from the Companies Registry, at a cost per company.

items.q: Can shareholders buy and sell shares between them?
items.a: Yes, with the secondary market, which is an add-on module.

items.q: Does it work for companies in Latin America?
items.a: The platform adapts to each country's terminology: shareholder ledger, general shareholders' meeting, board of directors. Compliance with each country's regulations is assessed case by case.
